Title: Oral citrulline supplementation protects female mice from the development of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD).

Journal/Date: European journal of nutrition (2017)

MeSH Keywords: Alanine Transaminase, Animals, Aspartate Aminotransferases, Biomarkers, Body Weight, Citrulline, Diet, Western, Dietary Supplements


--- ABSTRACT ---
[PURPOSE]: Impairments of intestinal barrier function are discussed as risk factors for the development and progression of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD). Studies suggest an association between arginine/citrulline homeostasis and the development of liver damages. Here, the effect of an oral L-citrulline (Cit) supplement on the development of a Western-style diet (WSD)-induced NAFLD was determined in mice.
[METHODS]: Female 6- to 8-week-old C57BL/6J mice were either pair-fed a liquid Western-style or control diet (C) ± 2.5 g/kg bodyweight Cit for 6 weeks (C + Cit or WSD + Cit). Indices of liver damage, glucose metabolism, intestinal barrier function and NO synthesis were measured.
[RESULTS]: While bodyweight gain was similar between groups, markers of glucose metabolism like fasting blood glucose and HOMA index and markers of liver damage like hepatic triglyceride levels, number of neutrophils and plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 protein levels were significantly lower in WSD + Cit-fed mice when compared to WSD-fed mice only. Protein levels of the tight junction proteins occludin and zonula occludens-1 in duodenum were significantly lower in mice fed a WSD when compared to those fed a WSD + Cit (-~70 and -~60 %, respectively, P < 0.05), whereas portal endotoxin levels, concentration of 3-nitrotyrosine protein adducts in duodenum and toll-like receptor-4 mRNA expression in livers of WSD + Cit-fed mice were markedly lower than in WSD-fed mice (-~43 %, P = 0.056; -~80 and -~48 %, respectively, P < 0.05).
[CONCLUSION]: Our data suggest that the protective effects of supplementing Cit on the development of NAFLD in mice are associated with a decreased translocation of endotoxin into the portal vein.

[CONCLUSION]: Our data suggest that the protective effects of supplementing Cit on the development of NAFLD in mice are associated with a decreased translocation of endotoxin into the portal vein.

key_findings.finding: A directly relevant prevention study found that oral L-citrulline protected female mice against Western-style-diet-induced NAFLD: 6–8-week-old female C57BL/6J mice were pair-fed a liquid Western-style diet or control diet, with or without 2.5 g/kg body weight citrulline, for 6 weeks. Compared with Western-style diet alone, the WSD+citrulline group had significantly lower hepatic triglycerides, hepatic neutrophil numbers, and PAI-1 protein; the authors concluded citrulline protected against NAFLD development.
